hook.line: In a hard conversation you sometimes need to plant your feet: I'm not moving until something changes. Spanish has a firm way to say it, and it has an extra *no* that trips English speakers.
hook.es: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
hook.en: I'm not starting until you pay me.

examples.es: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
examples.en: I'm not starting until you pay me.

examples.es: No me voy hasta que no lo vea.
examples.en: I'm not leaving until I see it.

examples.es: Hasta que no llegue el jefe, no se firma nada.
examples.en: Nothing gets signed until the boss arrives.

examples.es: No firmo hasta que no me expliquen todo.
examples.en: I won't sign until they explain everything to me.

examples.es: Hasta que no hablemos, no me quedo tranquila.
examples.en: I won't feel calm until we talk. (a woman speaking)

examples.es: No vamos a seguir hasta que no nos digan la verdad.
examples.en: We're not going on until they tell us the truth.

rule:
After *hasta que* ("until") Spanish often adds a *no* that changes nothing. *Hasta que no me pagues* means exactly *hasta que me pagues*. Don't translate it as "until you don't pay me".

The real "no" is in the main part: *no empiezo*, *no me voy*.

The verb after it takes the wish form (*pagues*, *vea*, *llegue*), because the thing hasn't happened yet.

It sets a boundary: I won't move until X. Both versions, with or without the extra *no*, are normal.
smallPrint: Teachers call this extra *no* an expletive or redundant negative. The verb after *hasta que* is in the present subjunctive when the event is still ahead.

readAndPick.es: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
options: I'm not starting until you pay me.
I'm not starting until you don't pay me.
I'm starting once you pay me.

readAndPick.es: No me voy hasta que no lo vea.
options: I'm leaving because I don't see it.
I'm leaving once I see it.
I'm not leaving until I see it.

readAndPick.es: Hasta que no llegue el jefe, no se firma nada.
options: Nothing gets signed until the boss arrives.
Nothing was signed because the boss arrived.
Everything gets signed when the boss arrives.

readAndPick.es: No firmo hasta que me expliquen todo.
options: I'll sign as soon as they explain everything to me.
I won't sign until they explain everything to me.
I don't sign because they explain everything to me.

readAndPick.es: Hasta que no vengas, no abro el café.
options: I'm not opening the café if you come. (to a friend)
I'm not opening the café until you come. (to a friend)
I opened the café when you came. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Hasta que no hablemos, no me quedo tranquila.
options: I won't feel calm until we talk. (a man speaking)
I won't feel calm until we talk. (a woman speaking)
She won't feel calm until we talk.

readAndPick.es: No te perdono hasta que no me pidas perdón.
options: I won't forgive you until you apologise to me. (to a friend)
I forgive you even though you don't apologise to me. (to a friend)
I won't forgive you because you apologise to me. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: No vamos a seguir hasta que no nos digan la verdad.
options: We're going on until they tell us the truth.
We're going on because they told us the truth.
We're not going on until they tell us the truth.

readAndPick.es: Hasta que no termines, no hablamos de otra cosa.
options: We won't talk about anything else until you finish. (to a friend)
We talk about something else when you finish. (to a friend)
We didn't talk about anything else because you finished. (to a friend)

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *llegue* or *llega* and type the whole sentence: *Hasta que no ___ el jefe, no se firma nada.*
yourTurn.answer: Hasta que no llegue el jefe, no se firma nada.
accept: Hasta que llegue el jefe, no se firma nada.
yourTurn.why: The boss hasn't arrived yet, so the verb takes the wish form, *llegue*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm not leaving until I see it.
yourTurn.answer: No me voy hasta que no lo vea.
accept: No me voy hasta que lo vea.
yourTurn.why: The first *no* is the real one; the second is optional and changes nothing.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm not starting until you pay me. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
accept: Hasta que me pagues, no empiezo.
No empiezo hasta que no me pagues.
No empiezo hasta que me pagues.
yourTurn.why: Wish form *pagues* for the thing that hasn't happened, and a real *no* before *empiezo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I won't sign until they explain everything to me.
yourTurn.answer: No firmo hasta que no me expliquen todo.
accept: No firmo hasta que me expliquen todo.
Hasta que no me expliquen todo, no firmo.
Hasta que me expliquen todo, no firmo.
yourTurn.why: *Expliquen* is the wish form for *ellos*, because the explaining is still ahead.

yourTurn.prompt: Drop the extra *no*: *No me voy hasta que no lo vea.* Say it the other natural way.
yourTurn.answer: No me voy hasta que lo vea.
yourTurn.why: The second *no* is only decoration, so the meaning stays the same without it.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about *we*: *No empiezo hasta que no lleguen todos.* Say: We're not starting until everyone arrives.
yourTurn.answer: No empezamos hasta que no lleguen todos.
accept: No empezamos hasta que lleguen todos.
yourTurn.why: Only the main verb changes to *empezamos*; the time part keeps its wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I won't forgive you until you apologise to me. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: No te perdono hasta que no me pidas perdón.
accept: No te perdono hasta que me pidas perdón.
Hasta que no me pidas perdón, no te perdono.
Hasta que me pidas perdón, no te perdono.
yourTurn.why: *Pidas* is the wish form for *tú*: you haven't apologised yet.

pitfalls.wrong: No me voy hasta que lo veo.
pitfalls.right: No me voy hasta que lo vea.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The seeing hasn't happened yet, so the verb takes the wish form, *vea*, not *veo*.

pitfalls.wrong: Hasta que no me pagues, empiezo.
pitfalls.right: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
pitfalls.why: The *no* after *hasta que* is only decoration; the real *no* belongs on the main verb, just like "I won't start until...".

pitfalls.wrong: Hasta no me pagues, no empiezo.
pitfalls.right: Hasta que no me pagues, no empiezo.
pitfalls.why: Keep the *que*: it is *hasta que*, and then the extra *no*.

personal: Set one honest boundary of your own and finish the line: *No empiezo hasta que no...* For example, *No hablo hasta que no tome mi tinto.*
